s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions with characteristic morphology and distribution
salient_findings: Intensely pruritic skin lesions on anterior thighs
Lesions have annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing and purpuric edges
Symmetric, mirror-image distribution on anterior thighs
key_facts: 6-year-old girl with no relevant medical history
Lesions first appeared 2 weeks earlier
Lesions occur in recurrent 3-day outbreaks
Lesions resolve spontaneously without residual injury
No systemic symptoms
No preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications
Laboratory studies are within normal limits
Lesions have well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on anterior thighs

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, matching the patient's skin lesions

shortlist.label: Urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent, intensely pruritic skin lesions, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques, matching the patient's skin lesions

shortlist.label: Annular erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetrically distributed lesions on the anterior thighs, consistent with the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric edges on the lesions, which could be indicative of vasculitis

raw.rationale: The patient's lesions have a characteristic annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology with central clearing, which is consistent with Erythema annulare centrifugum. The lesions also occur in recurrent outbreaks and resolve spontaneously, which is typical of this condition.

rejected.label: Urticaria
rejected.why: Urticaria typically presents with wheals that are more transient and migratory, whereas the patient's lesions are well-defined and persistent.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema multiforme often presents with target lesions and is associated with systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Annular erythema
rejected.why: Annular erythema is a broader term that encompasses several conditions, including Erythema annulare centrifugum, but the specific characteristics of the patient's lesions are more consistent with Erythema annulare centrifugum.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis typically presents with purpuric lesions and is associated with laboratory abnormalities, which are not present in this case.
